If they differ, they come out null or 0. (2) --setting-sources does not switch off managed settings (/etc/claude-code), so a managed hook could add noise; the hook_starts count and the log would show it. (3) The harness's session transcripts land under ~/.claude/projects (no --no-session-persistence, per the contract). (4) A model that retries after a deny makes hook_starts > 1 and the offsets ambiguous; the README says so. (5) CLAUDE* removal also drops any CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, so the login must come from ~/.claude credentials or ANTHROPIC_*; if it fails, stderr_head will show it. lessons: communicate() waits for the pipes to close, so a hook left running with the session's pipes open would stretch the session's wall time. The script times the process exit and drains the pipes in threads instead, and records pipes_open_10s_after_exit. Where a limit is hit, read session_end_after_hook_start_s next to last_tick_offset_s. proposed_decisions: (a) Use --hook-events (off by default, beyond the contract) for one extra run of pre-deny-60 to see the harness's own hook-outcome message; confidence medium, since the event's shape is unknown. (b) Project folders are per case and run (-), not per case, so a hook left running by run a cannot write into run b's log; this is a deliberate deviation from "one project per case", confidence high. (c) The .pid file is removed when the session ends, so a stale pid cannot be reused; confidence high. unresolved: Every case is unmeasured. Whether the harness's real limit at "timeout": 60 is 60 s, and whether a refusal after the limit is lost, is what the lead's runs measure.
